they are there listed in as saddhā, hiri, ottappa, viriya, paññā; by relying on (nissāya) them one akusalaṃ pajahati kusalaṃ bhāveti; in Bodhisattvas are described as sarvapraṇidhāna-niśraya-vigata, for whom all basis for (further) praṇidhānas is removed (because they are already perfect in praṇidhānas, as stated in and substantially in, along with niśrayasaṃpanna); app. support (of life; Tib. rten); in ˚yaḥ (Tib. gnas), of the four technical ‘requisites’ or supports, supplies, which a Buddhist monk needs and is allowed, listed as vṛkṣamūlam (for sleeping), piṇḍapātaḥ (for food), pāṃsukūlaṃ (for garments), pūtimukta- (q.v.) -bhaiṣajyam (for medicine); the same four in Pali (nissaya); in this sense niśrayadāyaka, m., a giver of …,; in also four, the list in 3—5 is (1) cīvara-, (2) piṇḍapāta-, (3) śayanāsanaṃ, and (4) glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāś ca; for nuns there are only three of these niśraya, since living in the woods, ‘at the foot of a tree’, is forbidden to them (); hence trayo niśrayā(ḥ); na ca skandha-āyatana-dhātau (one cpd. word) niśrayu tubhya vidyati kadācit (vs), reliance (dependence) on (the external world), the being based on (it); in (Tib. gnas or rten) the context suggests residence, fixed abode (between āspadam and niketaḥ); in tatra na śikṣā na niśrayo nāniśrayaḥ, the exact mg. is not too clear, and Tib. as printed in ed. omits this phrase; perhaps as in niśraya-saṃpanna, above, there is no instruction, no support and no non-support (for moral development) (?); Chin. no keeping nor not keeping of the moral code; niśrayāhṛta (lābha), received thru support,, explained

The interpretation of the name is correctly given by, and supported by the paraphrase paranirmitodyukta.

= prec., in a vs, doubtless a paraphrase to fit the meter:; interesting because the mg., devoted to (zealous for) the (enjoyments) magically created by others, confirms the interpretation of paranirmitavaśavartin.

, needing to be guided by others (on account of blindness): (prose) and (prose), both times ˚prāṇeya (with both mss. and one, also v.l.), interpreted as whose life (prāṇa) depends on others; (vs) ˚praṇeyeṣu (em. ˚yyeṣu), here short a in ˚praṇ˚ is required by meter; that ʼs theory is incorrect seems to me proved by where the persons in question say that, being blind, they cannot go anywhere vinā praṇetareṇa, without a guide.
, m. (= Pali parappavāda), rival (false, heretical) doctrine: nihatāḥ ˚dā(ḥ) (vs); in (vs) read parapravādān for paraṃ pra˚ (Tib. phas kyi rgol, see next);.

(prec. plus -in; not recorded in Pali), false teacher, one who promulgates false doctrine: = Tib. phas kyi rgol ba, which seems the usual term; ˚dy-anabhibhūta, said of Bodhisattvas, Tib. here pha rol gyi rgol ba;;;;;;;;;; (sarvaparapravādy-akampanatayā);;, etc. See also para-vādin.

, indecl. (nowhere recorded; Skt. paramam is so used), particle of assent, esp. to a command, assuredly, certainly:;;;;;; in (prose) parameti, with all his mss., read surely param iti with Calc., supported in sense by Tib.; a verb eti is not construable, and paramaṃ ti (for iti), or paramam iti, would be much less probable emendations.
, m. or nt., a high number: ˚masya. Corresponds to mapara, nt., mavara, also savara (2), qq.v.

(nt.), thought(s) of others, known to a Buddha by his supernatural knowledge: jātakā-paramateṣu kovidā (sc. Buddhas); sarvaparamataṃ viduḥ; see full discussion of both passages s.v. jātaka (3); misunderstands.

, supreme quality of the paramā bodhi, supreme enlightenment of a Buddha; there are seven such, (they are in no way related to the pāramitā), viz., āśraya-, pratipatti-, saṃpatti-, jñāna-, prabhāva-, prahāṇa-, and vihāra-p˚, defined in the following.

, nt., or ˚trā, f., a high number: = Tib. gzhal thag; cited from; in ˚mantrāyā(ḥ), gen. sg. fem.; corresponds to paramātra, q.v.; ˚mantraśaḥ (vs), by ʼs em. [Page319-b] which is prob. right (mss. mostly ˚mantiṇo, one good ms. ˚mantriśo).

, m., (cited from), or ˚praveśānugatā, (in both foll. by nāma gaṇanā), lit. (following) the entrance (penetration) into ultimate atom-dust, n. of a high number or method of computation (gaṇanā). Tib. on both rdul phra rab la ḥjug pa (in adding rjes su soṅ ba = anugata).
, m., = paramantra:, also = Tib. gzhal thag, which suggests that Tib. read ˚mātra rather than ˚mantra (gzhal, measure).
, m., n. of a Buddhist work:.
(see s.v. saṃvṛti 2), n. of a Buddhist work:.
, nt. (= Pali id.), eating (alms-food, on the part of monks) in (chosen) sequence, by (chosen) turns: (a sin, unless the monk is sick, or robes are to be given at one house; cf.).
, m. or nt., a high number:. Corresponds to dhavara, q.v.
, n. of a nāga king:. Cf. Maravāla.
(= Pali id.) = parapravādin, q.v.: mathiya (most mss. pathiya, but cf. Pali paravādivādamathanaṃ) ˚di (acc. pl.) (vs); ˚dibhir (prose).

, adj. Bhvr. (cf. Pali andhaveṇi paraṃparāsaṃsattā; Skt. saṃsakta, ppp., with parasparaṃ, adv., s.v. sañj with sam, 4), connected with one another, succeeding one another, of kings: te ca ˚tinaḥ … mahārājānaḥ (prose); if not corrupt, parasparā may be a blend of the adv. ˚ram with the noun paraṃparā, both Skt.
(Skt. only ger. ˚kṛṣya and ppp. ˚kṛṣṭa, once each in; not noted elsewhere), draws away: = Tib. phar ḥdren.
, aphetic form of aparādha, offence (): deśikaś ca parādhāparāddhaḥ (prose; no v.l.).
, f. ˚ikā, doubtful reading in several passages, listed s.v. aparāntaka.]
, m. (vv.ll. pārāp˚, pārāvata, both Skt., see on the first; parāpata with no v.l.), pigeon: = Tib. phug ron.

, condition of knowing successive states: pudgala-(mss. puṅgala-)parāparajñatā-kuśalo; (?) indriya-˚tā, so without report of v.l.; but very differently, omitting this word, acc. to the note with their ms. Ḱ and Tib.
, nt. (n. act. to next), the putting to flight: sarvamārabala-abhibhavana-˚ṇaṃ (so read, cpd.), conquest and putting to flight of all Māraʼs host.
(ppp. to ˚karoti, noted only in this and ˚karaṇa, preceding; cf. next), put to flight, routed: jitā bhagnāḥ parājitāḥ ˚kṛtā(ḥ); in virtually identical list, ˚kṛta(ḥ).

(cf. prec.; cpd. of parā with pṛṣṭhībhavati, q.v.), turns oneʼs back; in simple, literal sense, nirgacchantaṃ ˚bhūtvā, as he was going away (from the house) turning his back (to it); turns away (in disgust) from (someone deemed unworthy), ˚bhūtaḥ, of a Bodhisattva, from greedy people; resumed in -vimukhyasya (so mss., ed. em. vai˚) 15—16.
, m. (to next; = Pali parāmāsa), clinging to; see dṛṣṭi-p˚ and śīlavrata-p˚.

(= Pali ˚masati; in Skt. seems not used in same mgs.), cleaves or adheres to, takes up or is attached to (in an unworthy, disapproved way): śīlaṃ … na parāmṛśati srotaāpannaḥ, does not adhere to moral rules (in an unenlightened way, as the sequel explains; see śīlavrataparāmarśa);; mā … samyaksaṃbodhiṃ rūpataḥ (etc.) parāmṛkṣaḥ, do not attach yourself (cleave) to enlightenment as form (etc.); followed; by aparāmṛṣṭā (q.v.) hi … sarvajñatā, for omniscience is unattached (not unworthily affected, untarnished). See also parāmṛṣṭa.

(ppp. of prec.; = Pali ˚maṭṭha; cf. a-parā˚), (unworthily) adhered to: (= Pali) śrāmaṇyaṃ duṣparāmṛṣṭam evilly adhered to; the next vs 5 is a secondary imitation of this, and only as such has śrāmaṇyaṃ suparā˚, well or properly adhered to (su-parā˚ is really a contradiction in terms, as if one said ‘a righteous infatuation’);. [In = parāmṛṣṭa = considered, deliberate, a Skt. mg. of the verb; so Tib. indicates; ms. paramṛṣṭa, ed. wrongly em. parimuṣṭa, cf. Pali. The whole vs is substantially right in text of, wrong in.]
, f. (= parāmarśa: to parāmṛśati, q.v.), (unworthy, disapproved) adherence, clinging to:;;.

, adj. (or subst., nt.; Skt. parāyaṇa plus -īya), that which has … as its goal; what tends towards … as its goal or refuge: likhāpanīyaṃ bodhi-parāyaṇīyaṃ (delete daṇḍa or transpose it to here); bodhiparāyaṇaṃ niyataṃ, what tends to the goal (or refuge) of enlightenment is to be depicted; (then) the goal (refuge) of enlightenment is certain.

, ppp., and parāvṛtti, n. act. (both Skt.), reversed, and reversion, revulsion, of the basic mentality (esp. called āśraya, q.v., in,); technically of the fundamental change in mental attitude which is taught as necessary to knowledge of the true doctrine: parāvṛttāśraya (text ˚vṛtā˚); cf.; parāvṛtty-āśraya, having the basis (of consciousness) characterized by (this) revulsion (or read ˚vṛttāśra˚ ?); parāvṛtta, e.g.; ˚tti; for others see; also in, see; (*20, *24).
, nt. (to next; here domal ṇ), beating (of a drum, here the ‘drum of the law’): mahādharmabherī- ˚naṃ (prose).

(also ˚ṇati), ˚hanti (not recorded in MIndic; in Skt. not in this mg.; cf. parāhaṇana), strikes; esp. a drum (bherī, dundubhi, either lit., or fig. dharma-bh˚, du˚, the drum of the law): ˚hananti (read ˚tī m.c.);; ˚haṇe, 1 sg. opt.,; ˚hanasva (˚hanāhi); ˚haniṣyati; ˚haniṣyasi; ˚ghnanto, pple.,; ˚hanantaṃ; ˚hanyamānair, pass. pres. pple.,; ˚hatā; a gong (gaṇḍī), ˚hatya, ger.,; vāditrabhāṇḍāni parāhatāni; (piṇḍapātaṃ) parāhatya; the earth (mahī, pṛthivī, dharaṇī) ˚hanti; ˚hanati; ˚hatya; ˚hanitvā (vs).
, m. (mss.; ˚ḍḍhaka; to next, plus -aka), leader, manager, ruler: (of a flock of birds); (of deer). Cf. parikarṣaka.
(mss.; ˚kaḍḍhati; see Chap. 43 s.v. kaṭṭ-ati; in mg. = Skt. pari-kṛṣ), leads, governs, manages, said of the leader of a flock of deer: ˚ti.

(= Pali id., both senses; Skt. Lex. only), [Page320-b] (1) roundabout talk; indirect allusion (see s.v. avabhāsa):; (2) more generally, talk, perhaps lengthy speech: (vs) parikatha bhikṣu yadī na bhārasaṃjñā, if a (long) tale does not seem to you a burden; but takes parikatha as 2 sg. impv. to ˚kathayati; Tib. dge sloṅ (= bhikṣu) khur gyi ḥdu śes (notion of burden) med (not) na (= yadi) gsuṅs (speak; verb or noun ?); more especially of a religious talk, sermon or dialogue,; (bhikṣavo …) ˚thāṃ kurvanti.
(nt.; to next, plus -ana), help, assistance, service: paraduḥkheṣu parikaraṇakuśalāś ca (of Bodhisattvas).
(= Pali id.; possibly denom. to Skt. parikara; cited ˚karoti, but all its citations fit the stem in -a-), aids, serves, waits upon: (mātaraṃ pitaraṃ …) parikared (prose).

,, acc. to Index, prayer (?); but rather speech of preparation (Skt. parikarma), sc. for religious life: (mayā …, Buddha speaking of his past existences) evaṃvidhā parikarmakathā kṛtā yad … prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi gṛhāśramam apahāya ṛṣayaḥ pravrajitvā etc.)

, nt., n. sg. ˚ṇaṃ, = parikarma (), or n. act. to Skt. parikarmayati with -ana, working over, preparation (of Bodhisattvas, compared to jewels): buddhorasānāṃ parikarmaṇaṃ tathā (vs; cf. vaiḍūryaratne parikarma niyaṃte, read nīyate, line 6).
(Skt. parikarma-n plus kar-; = Skt. parikarmayati), works up, makes ready: ˚kuru.
, m. (to Skt. parikarṣati; cf. parikaṭṭaka), one who controls, manages: (dvāv agrāmātyau …) rāja-parikarṣakau rājaparipālakau.

, nt. (not noted in these mgs.), (1) carrying about in the mind, thinking on, planning: idam agraṃ vyāpādānāṃ yad utānantarya-parikarṣaṇam. Acc. to, a parallel text has ānantaryopakramaṇam; Tib. cited as byed par śom pa, preparing to commit; (2) (cf. Pali parikaḍḍhati, in this sense) attracting, drawing to oneself: svapakṣa-parikarṣaṇākāraṃ, having the form of attracting (drawing to oneself) oneʼs own allies (presumably ‘good friends’ who help one in the right path); parikarṣaṇārthaṃ bālānāṃ = (vs), for the sake of drawing the simple-minded to myself.

, (1) (= Skt. parikarṣati, carries around; in Skt. karṣayati is used in the sense of karṣati) carries around (a child, said of a nurse):, see s.v. aṅkadhātrī; (2) perhaps attracts, draws to oneself (see s.v. parikarṣaṇa, 2): (buddhavaṃśam anudhārayiṣyasi dharmavaṃśa pariśodhayiṣyasi) saṃghavaṃśa parikarṣayiṣyase (vs). Or can the word here mean you will support, nurse, carry around the Order (as a nurse carries a child; above)?

, m. (not in Skt., except rarely Jain Skt., see, where it is rendered Täuschung; Pali parikappa, acc. to assumption, supposition, surmise; once,, said to mean preparation, intention, strategem, but at least as possible would be vain, false imaginings for parikappehi there), fundamentally (1) surmise, assumption, hypothesis, figment of imagination, regularly with implication of falsity or unreliability (cf. parikalpayati); sometimes of an innocent hypothesis or frankly imaginary assumption: parikalpam upādāya;, assuming a hypothetical case, to take an imaginary hypothesis; but chiefly with derogatory implication, vain fancy, as something to be got rid of; often with kalpa and vikalpa, qq.v.; sarva-kalpa-vikalpaparikalpa-prahāṇāya; na kalpo na vikalpo na parikalpaḥ; kalpavikalpa-parikalpa- [Page321-a] (prose; Tib. omits the equivalent of parik˚, doubtless by haplography); parikalpa-saṃjña-vigatā(ḥ) (vs); (avikalpe bodhisattvajñānamaṇḍale) sarva-kalpa-parikalpā na saṃvidyate (= ˚yante; read so ?); sukham atra (sc. gṛhāvāse) kutaḥ kathaṃ kadā vā parikalpapraṇayaṃ na ced upaiti, whence, how, and when could there be happiness in this (householderʼs life), if (as has been shown in the prec. vs) it does not come to one who is devoted to vain imaginings? (otherwise); abhūta-(q.v.)-parikalpa-; abhūta-parikalpasamutthitaś ca (said of the body), arisen from unreal imaginings; -parikalpa-samutthita-; parikalpa-samucchrita (vs), produced by vain imaginings, said of kāmaguṇāḥ, which are called māyamarīci-samā(ḥ) and the like in the same vs; parikalpasamucchritaḥ (-samutthitaḥ); Tib. here yoṅs su rtogs pa, and regularly so or with rtog (pa) for rtogs (pa), as in and (but in rtogs); this is a woodenly literal rendering; yoṅs su = pari, while kalpa is rendered rtog(s pa), defined consider, reflect, discern, perceive, understand (the distinction between rtog and rtogs which sets up is clearly not maintained in the texts); the derogatory connotation is recognized s.v. rtog pa by and, yet erroneously renders the cpd. yoṅs su rtogs pa las byuṅ ba, ‘having arisen from quite reliable information (parikalpa-samucchriti)’; vikalpa is rendered rnam par rtog(s) pa; (2) nt. or m., prose version of a jātaka or legend; four times in colophons of, always at the end of prose accounts; in the first three followed by verse accounts of the same story: parikalpa-padaṃ; samāptaṃ śyāmakajātakasya parikalpaṃ; samāptaṃ hastinikājātakasya parikalpaṃ; padumāvatīye parikalpo samāpto (v.l. ˚paṃ samāptaṃ) (here not followed by any version in verse).

(cf. prec.), imagines or distinguishes falsely: ˚payan, pres. pple.,; ˚pita, ppp.,; ˚pita as one of the three svabhāva, q.v., wrongly imagined,;; explained; with lakṣaṇa, 3, q.v., instead of svabhāva, ˚pita-lakṣaṇam; (: indice imaginaire).
, adj., in a-pari˚, (not) desiring:, see s.v. nirvṛti 2. (There is a v.l. a-pratikāṅkṣ˚.)
(pari plus denom. from kīla, stake, cf. Skt. kīlita), puts stakes around (a tree, for protection): (so dāni taṃ) nyagrodhapotaṃ … parikhaneti parikīleti parikuddāleti (? see this).
, abusing, reviling: ˚kāḥ, v.l. of and for parivādakāḥ and 12 anukuṭṭakāḥ.
, perhaps to be read in (see parikuddāleti), walls about (?).

, so for his text parikuḍḍāleti; he assumes pari plus denom. from Skt. kuddāla, hoes or spades around (a tree):, see parikīleti. But the mss. read ˚kudeti or ˚kūḍyeti, which looks more like a denom. from kuḍya (Lex. also kūḍya), wall; perhaps walls about?

, read prob. pari-kūḍyate, (pass. of pari with kūḍ-, kūl-, qq.v. in), is roasted: (iha te) bālāḥ parikrūḍyante (all mss. -kr-, but read ˚kūḍ˚) sūnākāṣṭheṣv (most mss. śūnā˚; read śūlā˚) ivorabhrāḥ (prose), in this (life) fools are roasted all around (turned over fires) like rams on spits (lit. spit-sticks).

, ifc. Bhvr. (= Skt. parigha, Pali usually paligha, once palikha,, where kh is explained as dialectic for gh; another possible explanation would [Page321-b] be confusion with Skt. and Pali parikhā, ditch, trench), obstacle; chiefly in cpd. utkṣipta-p˚, with obstacles removed: (prose), em. ˚parikheda, but mss. clearly tho corruptly point to ˚parikha, confirmed by;; also udīrṇa-p˚.
(= Pali pali˚; Skt. only ger. parikhāya, once in, see), digs up, roots out: (mūlaṃ) parikhanya (em., but confirmed by same line in Pali with palikhāya,; one ms. palikhan-, perhaps read so).
, m., house: = Tib. khaṅ khyim;. Orig. doubtless attendants, household, like Skt. parijana.
(to ˚gaveṣate plus -ana), act of searching for: ˚ṣaṇāvipravasitenāśayena (so read, 2d ed., see vipravasati).
, read prob. ˚ṣaṇa-tā, or possibly ˚ṣaṇā, f.; = prec.: citta-parigaveṣa-tāye (loc.; so text), see next.

, rarely ˚ti (this cpd. of Skt. gaveṣate is recorded only in BHS; cf. prec. two), searches all round for, looks intently for (acc.): kumāraṃ ˚ṣamāṇaḥ; gṛhapatiṃ parimārgati ˚veṣati; arthān parimārgate ˚veṣate; -devatāṃ ˚veṣamāṇo; ˚ṣamāṇa-; cittaṃ ˚veṣate, looks hard for, tries to find (inquires into, but the sequel shows that the point is that the citta cannot be found however hard one searches for it); this is cited; ātmanaḥ parigaveṣyamāṇānupalambhāt (pres. passive pple.).
, adj., greedy, grasping:;;; a-parigṛddha-cetasaḥ; see paliguddha, and parigredha.

, ppp. (in mg. comprehended, ˚taṃ bodhisattvaiḥ, may be regarded as standard Skt., where at least close relatives of this word are so used), ungenerous, close-fisted, stingy, in neg. a-pari˚: amātsaryo 'haṃ (Buddha speaks) kulaputrā aparigṛhītacitto … buddhajñānasya dātā, I am, gentlemen, one who gives out the Buddha-knowledge without selfishness, with heart not niggardly (restricted); Tib. ḥdzin pa (= parigṛhīta; note that zin pa, a form of the same Tib. verb, renders parigṛddha, q.v.) sems (= citta) med do (I am not). The word of course is not connected with parigṛddha; Skt. parigṛhīta has mgs. like limited, restricted, of which this is a specialization.

, in tripauruṣa-parigohyāni, is or represents a word meaning circumference (epithet of iṣikāni, so ed., see iṣika); mss. corrupt, see. The same word, whatever it was, should surely be read as final member of the word read by tripauruṣoccāni (see s.v. udvedha).

, nt. (Skt. only masc.), property: (vs), here predicate noun to subj. gṛham, neut.; perhaps by assimilation of gender; (may be m. or nt.,) (saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma) dharmaparyāyaṃ … sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ … saṃprakāśayām āsa, perhaps which is the property of all the Buddhas (one Chin. transl. protected, guarded, or preserved by the Buddhas); vaipulyasūtrāṇa parigrahe (vs), in the acquisition of the … (substantially so used in Skt.).
, adj. or subst. m., completely grasping, comprehending (not recorded in this mg.): ˚kaḥ, mahāyāna-p˚; saddharma-p˚; pravacana-p˚.
, m. (= Pali paligedha; see paligodha, parigṛddha, and esp. s.v. gredha), greed: = Tib. yoṅs su zhen pa, extreme desire.
(caus. to pari plus ghar-, Skt. ghārayati; see s.v. gharati), moistens round about: (em. ˚ghār˚), after pariṣyandeti (and acc. to paryārdreti; mss. corrupt).
(cf. next three), (sexual) commerce: kutaḥ punar anayā sāṛdhaṃ ˚ṇā.
